## devops/governance-lock-lifecycle
--- DROPPED LINES (present in pre-sync repo, absent in deployed) ---
< - **A bare `check_lock()` is not a status check.** Called with no args it cannot resolve the session
<   and returns `{"active": false}` while the lock is live on disk. When the file says active and the
<   no-arg call says inactive, **the file is right** — the close will succeed. Do not re-acquire, do not
<   open a carrier cycle; that false negative manufactures the very extra cycle you were trying to avoid.
--- ADDED LINES (deployed-only) ---
> - **`advance_task_state` is also the recovery for a lock stranded by a CRASHED close.** A close that raises after `feedback_accept` leaves the cycle scored-but-PENDING with the lock still held, and a repeated `end_change` throws again rather than clearing it. A terminal transition (`new_state="cancelled"`) releases it — the tool reports "a terminal task holds nothing" — and records the reason in `task_events`. Use that instead of a force/override, and say plainly in the reason what crashed, because the range then has no receipt and the next close must mint one.
> - **Read the lock's FULL picture; `active` alone is only YOUR lock.** A call with no args cannot
>   resolve a session, so `active` reports `false` while another session's lock is live on disk — that
>   field answers "do *I* hold a lock", never "is any lock held". The call also returns `locks` +
>   `live_lock_count` listing every live lock (task, session, agent, repo, heartbeat): read those before
>   concluding none exists, and when the lock FILE says active while `active` says false, **the file is
>   right** — the close will succeed. Do not re-acquire and do not open a carrier cycle; that false
>   negative manufactures the very extra cycle you were trying to avoid.

## devops/loop-governance
--- DROPPED LINES (present in pre-sync repo, absent in deployed) ---
< - **Complexity is measured, never self-reported** — computed from the session's actual git diff: ≥50 lines (added+removed counted separately) or ≥3 files (non-noise); touching an always-review path (`plugins/governance-enforcer/`, `mcp-servers/loop-gov-mcp.py`, `core/governance/`, `ops/scripts/pre-commit-score`, `pre-push-pull`, `post-commit-audit`, `post-push-audit`, `ops/scripts/cortex-update.sh`, `ops/scripts/quality/adversarial-verify.py`, `.hermes-cortex/hooks/`) gates regardless of size. Uncommitted work counts (staged + unstaged + untracked — no "create big file, don't add, dodge"); exact-name lockfiles (`Cargo.lock`, `package-lock.json`, …) are discounted, checked AFTER always-review paths. Trivial changes skip review.
< - **Reviewer independence** — the reviewer runs in the MCP daemon with a distinct model (default `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, override `ADVERSARIAL_REVIEWER_MODEL`) and a fixed, committed orchestrator-owned prompt (`docs/templates/adversarial-reviewer-prompt.md`, deployed copy `~/.hermes-cortex/templates/`); the worker can neither invoke nor edit it. A same-agent/same-model self-review is a self-report, not an evaluation. Reviewer input is treated as untrusted data; the worker's `feedback_accept` note is passed as the self-report being reviewed.
--- ADDED LINES (deployed-only) ---
> - **Print each case BY NAME, not just a total.** An aggregate "ALL PASS (N tests)" is a claim
>   about an execution the reviewer cannot see, and it gets filed as one: they ask which cases
>   produced the count. Have the check emit its own case lines (`A: absent interpreter -> named
>   path, rc=78`, `::test_<name> PASSED`) into the artifact, and prefer a runner that prints the
>   per-test names beside the summary. A count without its cases is the same defect as a summary
>   line from a piped `tail`.

--- ADDED LINES (deployed-only) ---
> - `⚠️ Repo clean` → establish WHAT is uncommitted before assigning it an owner. Several tracked
>   `docs/evidence/` files (`briefings/*`, `gateway-suite-results.txt`, and the drift detector's own
>   `skill-drift-parity.txt`) are REWRITTEN BY TEST RUNS and by the tools, so a dirty set of exactly
>   those is a byproduct of a suite run — not a peer's edit and not abandoned work. Prove it by
>   running the suite in a clean worktree of HEAD: the same files come back dirty there with no
>   session involved. For anything else, `git log -1 --format='%an %ae' -- <path>` gives authorship,
>   and another session's files are never committed, reverted or stashed on the strength of a dirty
>   listing alone.

## software-development/agent-contract
--- DROPPED LINES (present in pre-sync repo, absent in deployed) ---
< 10. **Stop before destruction** — get approval for data loss, security risk, privilege escalation.
< 16. **No PII in the repo** — public (MIT). Never commit real domains, home paths, emails, IPs, or hostnames; use placeholders. Enforcement: `secret-leak-detector.sh` blocks real emails in the public repo; the enforcer PII gate blocks real emails in skill/shared-surface writes.
--- ADDED LINES (deployed-only) ---
> 10. **Stop before destruction** — get approval for data loss, security risk, privilege escalation. A destructive command in a mid-flight or unattended path stalls on the approval gate and costs the turn, so when scratch state only needs to be FRESH, do not delete it: use a new unique path (`$WORK/probe-2/`) and build captures append-only. Once something is blocked, never rephrase or retry it toward the same outcome — switch to a non-destructive equivalent and carry on.
> 16. **No PII in the repo** — public (MIT). Never commit real domains, home paths, emails, IPs, or hostnames; use placeholders. Enforcement: `secret-leak-detector.sh` blocks real emails in the public repo; the enforcer PII gate blocks real emails in skill/shared-surface writes. **The gate also rejects what it cannot distinguish from PII, and that lands on TEST FIXTURES and docs, not just data.** A bare run of 8+ digits reads as a phone number (an epoch-style id, a timestamp constant, a long numeric fixture); a real first name or surname reads as a personal identifier. The write is refused with the offending lines quoted — rewrite the VALUE, never remove the field: use short placeholder ids (`cycle_id: 999`, `sid: "test-session"`), invented domains (`example.com`), and role words instead of names (`the-agent`). Fixing the fixture keeps the test meaningful; deleting the value quietly weakens it.
> 
> ### Reporting order — defects outrank ceremony
> 
> - **Fix first, report second; never let ceremony lead.** A status report that lists process items — notify the fleet, clean up scratch, update the docs — while the change's own defects are still open reads as avoidance, not diligence, and has drawn a direct rebuke. Lead with what is BROKEN or unproven. Process items go last, and only once nothing is broken.
> - **"Fixed" is a claim that requires a test failing without it.** A commit message or note describing a fix that was never written is worse than an open bug: the record says otherwise, so nobody looks again. If the code changed but nothing pins it, write "code changed, unverified" under `## Unverified` — do not write "fixed". Likewise never commit a red suite: gate the commit on the runner's own rc (`if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then git commit …; else echo "REFUSING: tests are red"; fi`), because a `;` chain commits the failure while looking disciplined.
> - **When asked what is left, answer with the inventory, not the wins.** Blocking state first, then known-and-unfixed defects, then unverified assumptions, then owed work. Completed work is context, never the answer.

## software-development/change-checklist
--- DROPPED LINES (present in pre-sync repo, absent in deployed) ---
<       even when the check passing was real.
--- ADDED LINES (deployed-only) ---
> - [ ] **Ambient environment is the same trap one level up: a test that reads HOME, CWD, or an
>       env var another module sets is a test whose verdict depends on who invoked it.** The
>       symptom is a test that passes alone and FAILS inside the full suite, where a sibling
>       module's `HOME` (or a leaked `CORTEX_*` var) is in effect — and it is easy to misread as
>       "my change broke it". Derive paths from the REPO under test (`Path(__file__).parents[1]`)
>       or pass them in explicitly; never from the ambient `HOME`/`CORTEX_REPO`. Prove it both
>       ways before shipping: run the file alone AND from a foreign directory with a foreign HOME
>       (`cd /tmp && HOME=/tmp/fakehome pytest <file>`), then assert the default roots

## software-development/hermetic-python-testing
--- DROPPED LINES (present in pre-sync repo, absent in deployed) ---
<   table, not the fixture, decides what is legal.
--- ADDED LINES (deployed-only) ---
> ### 9. The caller's environment can change WHICH tests exist — not just what they read
> 
> Rule 6's family, one level up. An inherited `PYTHONPATH` or `PYTHONHOME` that points at a
> foreign `site-packages` makes some test modules fail to IMPORT, and pytest then reports a
> smaller suite as a clean run. Measured on one host, same command, only the environment
> differing: **1818 collected with 4 collection errors** contaminated vs **1846 with none**
> clean — four whole modules dropped, and the runner printed `N passed` either way. An agent
> shell almost always exports `PYTHONPATH`, so the contaminated case is the DEFAULT case.

## software-development/prove-before-create
--- DROPPED LINES (present in pre-sync repo, absent in deployed) ---
< | Concept exists in one codebase but not another | Port it, don't rewrite it |
--- ADDED LINES (deployed-only) ---
> | Capability exists in one codebase but not another | Port it, don't rewrite it |
> | Capability exists only as a SKILL, bound to a system you are moving off | Port the capability to a system-neutral tool; say explicitly what the existing skill covers and what the gap actually is |
> | Capability is blocked by a runtime dependency the target hosts lack | Replace the dependency (e.g. compile the database engine in) rather than requiring a host install |
> 
> ## Choose the Implementation Stack by MEASURING the Host
> 
> Creating a new tool is also a choice of language, runtime, and dependencies — and that choice is a
> "create" decision with the same debt. **Measure before you pick; never adopt a suggested stack on
